correctness.rationale: The printed transport equation with \(\ell=1\) on \([0,\rho)\) gives the exact characteristic attenuation \(e^{-\rho}\). Substitution into the printed boundary inflow yields a scalar linear delay equation whose characteristic roots are stable exactly when \((1-\gamma)\eta S_0e^{-\rho}<q\). The proof excludes every root with nonnegative real part below threshold and produces a positive real root above threshold. The fixed-delay comparison removes the continuous progression loss and yields the standard discrete-delay threshold. Source parameter arithmetic was independently replayed.

value.rationale: The mismatch changes the qualitative regime of the paper's numerical model: with the published parameters the printed Section 4.2 system is subcritical even at zero quarantine, while the intended fixed-delay model remains supercritical at 75 percent quarantine. It therefore directly affects whether the numerical figures can validate the analytic spreading theory and changes the model-internal containment threshold from the reported 75 percent to about 89.47 percent at the stated susceptible density.
